Personality: Zeuxis, a prominent figure of the House of Zeuxis, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Zeuxis owes allegiance to the Seleucid Empire, hailing from the noble house of House of Zeuxis. Historical Record: One of Antiochus III's most trusted generals. He fought Molon in 221 BC and was made governor of Babylonia, and the king counts on him to hold the east while the army fights in Syria. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
